target_customer: Interventional radiologists and hospitals treating women with chronic pelvic pain from pelvic venous disorders
problem: Chronic pelvic pain affects millions of US women and current options are opioids or limited procedures. V-Flow targeted a venous root cause.
business_model: Regulated medical device sold to hospitals (pre-revenue, not yet cleared)
product_category: Medical device, venous catheter and stent system

founders.name: Peter Balmforth
founders.background_notes: Serial medtech entrepreneur per YC page

founders.name: Rodney Brenneman
previous_startups: More than half a dozen medical device startups
founders.background_notes: Mechanical engineer, 40+ years in device development, named inventor on over 100 patents. NIH grant principal investigator.

technical_complexity.rationale: A novel venous diagnostic catheter and modular stent need device design, animal studies and first-in-human trials before commercialization.

defensibility.rationale: The company claimed a broad IP portfolio and no competing IP for its indication, and FDA clearance would be a barrier, but the IP claim is self reported.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Medtronic and Cook sold embolization products for pelvic venous disorders, but no evidence found of acquiring or copying V-Flow.

market_need_then: The company cited over 15 million US women affected and 39 billion dollars annual cost, and the NIH HEAL initiative sought non-opioid pain treatments, per the company's YC description.

identity.voice_and_tone: Clinical and mission driven, aimed at women with chronic pain

brand_strength.rationale: No brand assets or press found, and the name is easily confused with Flow Medical, an unrelated company.

outcome_analysis: V-Flow Medical joined YC Summer 2021 with an experienced medtech team and a device aimed at pelvic venous causes of chronic pain. Its only funding found is a 2023 NIH grant of about 300 thousand dollars and it is now listed inactive. The cause of the inactivity is not public, so no failure factors are assigned.
notes: Status is Inactive per YC and aggregators, but exit type is unknown because no shutdown notice or cause was found (cause not public). Company website returned 403, treated as unreadable. NIH grant is a single source (a RePORTER derived page), no cross-check found. No private rounds found; family office investors are mentioned by one directory behind a paywall. Flow Medical (Chicago) is an unrelated company and its funding was excluded. No competitor sources dated near mid 2021 were found, so the list is empty.
